purpose: v9.3 coupling-weight sweep arm 'w025': the coupled pilot (render 2.0 / consistency 2.0) proved the mechanism (on-figure .68->.93 at 10k, = what uncoupled v9.0 needs 100k for) but taxed pixels (TVR .721 vs v9.0's ~.75 at 10k with far worse structure trend). This sweep asks whether a lower weight (0.25/0.5/1.0) or a 5k-step linear warmup of the full 2.0 weight keeps the fast rig-pixel binding without the pixel tax. Declared before any arm result. Primary judgment (declared here): (1) next-block divergence (eval/next_block_divergence.py, 32 clips, best-of-4, 6 blocks, seed 20260824) — teacher-forced best-of-N average, lower is better; (2) on-figure rate >= .85 at 10k (coupling must retain its binding gain); (3) TVR at 10k not worse than v9.0 10k control (.75). Winner = lowest teacher-forced divergence among arms passing (2) and (3); if no arm passes both, coupling is judged net-negative at 10k and the flagship recipe falls back to v9.0 + rig-drop. Matched controls: v9.0 10k (no coupling) and the coupled 2.0 pilot.
